title.en: Wide turns and inner slices on larger cubes

summary: Model a larger cube where a move addresses a contiguous range of layers and centre pieces carry individual identity even when they look interchangeable.
objective: Build a four-layer cube where outer block turns and inner slice turns are distinct legal moves with correct notation.
intent_signals: Show the difference between a wide turn and an outer face turn.
Model a 4x4 cube with correct move notation.
example_prompts: Build a 4x4 cube with wide turns and inner slice moves I can apply and undo.
Show which pieces an outer block move affects compared with a single-layer turn.
negative_signals: Not a solving method or parity-algorithm database for larger cubes.
Not a physical mechanism model: internal cores and cuttings are out of scope.
not_for: Not a solving method or parity-algorithm database for larger cubes.
Not a physical mechanism model: internal cores and cuttings are out of scope.

entities.name: Layer model
entities.guidance: Represent the cube as indexed layers per axis so a move can address a contiguous block of layers rather than a single face.

entities.name: Piece classes
entities.guidance: Distinguish corner, edge and centre piece classes explicitly, since larger cubes have multiple centres per face that are not individually fixed.

entities.name: Notation display
entities.guidance: Show the notation for each applied move alongside the layer block it turned, so notation and effect are checkable against each other.

state_contract.model: Exact discrete state over indexed layers per axis. A move is a face, a contiguous layer range measured from that face (start depth and count, so outer block moves are the special case starting at depth 1) and a turn amount, with declared legal ranges. Competition notation is used for outer block moves; an inner-only slice is expressed in the scene as its own notation and is equivalent to the difference of two outer blocks. A move history supports undo, and pending and committed move labels are separate.
state_contract.authority: The layer block definition is authoritative: an animation that rotates a different set of layers than the move declares is a defect.
actions: Apply a wide turn covering two layers.
Apply an inner slice turn only.
Undo the last move or reset to solved.

invariants: A move rotates exactly the contiguous layer range it declares: an outer block starts at the face, an inner slice starts deeper, and the animated block always matches the declared range.
Undo restores the exact prior state including centre piece positions.

Centre pieces are tracked individually in the exact state, so permuting same-coloured centres is a state change even though an unmarked puzzle looks identical; visual solvedness and state identity are reported separately.
motion_guidance: Animate the whole addressed block as one rigid rotation; animating layers separately would imply moves the model does not have.
Show the pending move label as the animation begins and move it to the committed history only when the state changes, so a cancelled or in-flight move is never recorded as executed.
known_limits: Notation conventions differ between sources and puzzle sizes; the scene must state which convention it implements.
Larger cubes introduce solving parity cases that this recipe does not address.
The cited regulations define outer block moves only; inner-only slice moves are a scene convention here, expressible as the difference of two outer blocks.
Authored guidance only: no scene runtime, rendering or numerical calibration has been run for this recipe.

claims.statement: Competition notation for cubes with more than three layers defines outer block moves in which an outer slice turns together with adjacent inner slices, written with the number of slices n to move in the range greater than one and less than the number of layers, with n omitted meaning two slices.
claims.scope: Outer block moves as published in the cited article, re-read in this session. The same document has no separate inner-slice article, so any inner-only slice notation used in a scene is that scene's own convention and must be declared as such.

source_refs.locator: Article 12a2, outer block moves and the range of n

object_craft.structure: Cubies of uniform size with visible gaps so layer boundaries are countable at a glance.
object_craft.material: Standard face palette with slightly varied value per centre piece so individual centres remain distinguishable.
object_craft.articulation: A move rotates a parented block of cubies about the face axis and reparents them on completion.

object_craft.structure: A move ticker anchored in the scene showing the current and previous moves.
object_craft.material: Monospaced opaque plate so notation stays legible against the puzzle.
object_craft.articulation: The ticker updates when a move commits, not when it starts animating.

physical_contract.scope: Exact discrete state with animated block rotation; no mechanism or contact simulation.
checks: Undo returns the exact previous state.
The animated block matches the layer count declared by the move.
